battery_overview: This page is Call 7 run from the defense's declared perspective — Shell USA, Inc. and Shell Chemical, L.P. The analytical output is identical to the prosecution's Call 7 source data, but the strategic interpretation is run with the defense's bias: their side, their concerns, their fears, and their read on opposing counsel. The purpose is to show the prosecution's team exactly how the defense reads this exchange — what they see as useful, what they fear, and how they rank the analytical calls. Because the model was run with Shell as the declared client, the raw score labels are swapped on display: what the model called client value (Shell's gain) is shown as Opposition Value, and what the model called opposition value (the plaintiff's gain) is shown as Client Value. Everything reads consistently from the prosecution's perspective across both SI views.
score_swap_note: Raw JSON: client_value = Shell's gain · opposition_value = plaintiff's gain. Displayed: Client Value = plaintiff's gain · Opposition Value = Shell's gain.

client_bias_declaration.what_you_are_afraid_of: Credible testimony of defendant safety failures
client_bias_declaration.opposing_counsel_read: Use expert to establish defendant safety failures

pattern_field.label: Pair Strategic Signature
pattern_field.definition: The two-to-three word strategic label naming what this pair means for the defense's case position. Generated from the defense's declared bias. This is not an analytical label — it names the strategic consequence from the opposing side's perspective: what the defense sees as the meaning of this exchange for their case.
pattern_field.why_it_matters: Reveals the defense's strategic read on this exchange — what they see as the consequence of this pair for their case position. Knowing how the defense labels this pair tells the prosecution's team what the opposition is thinking and where they will focus their energy.
pattern_field.value_description: The two-to-three word label shown is the defense's strategic judgment of what this pair means for Shell's case position — from their perspective, not the prosecution's.
pattern_field.null_explanation: A strategic signature could not be produced for this pair.

fields.label: Summary
fields.definition: A three-to-four sentence strategic overview from the defense's declared perspective. This is the defense's strategy brief — what happened in this exchange that matters to Shell, and what their attorneys should know before walking into or past this pair. All findings are drawn from battery output, not invented.
fields.why_it_matters: Shows the prosecution's team exactly how the defense reads this pair — what they think is useful, what they fear, and how they will frame their strategy. Understanding the opposing side's read on each pair is essential for anticipating and countering their moves.
fields.value_description: Written as three to four direct, opinionated sentences from the defense's perspective. Not a neutral description — the defense's strategy brief for this pair.
fields.null_explanation: A strategic summary could not be produced for this pair.

fields.label: Client Value (plaintiff's gain)
fields.definition: How useful this pair is to the plaintiff's side, as assessed by the defense model. This is the raw opposition_value field from the defense model run — the defense's own assessment of how much this pair benefits the plaintiff — displayed here as Client Value to normalize everything to the prosecution's perspective. A cross-check against the prosecution SI run's client_value score.
fields.why_it_matters: Shows how the defense model assessed the plaintiff's gain from this pair. When this score differs significantly from the prosecution SI run's client_value, it reveals a disagreement in strategic assessment between the two model runs — worth noting.
fields.scale_description: Scored from 0 to 10 — the defense model's assessment of how much this pair benefits the plaintiff's side. 0 means the defense sees no benefit to the plaintiff here. 10 means the defense sees this pair as a defining asset for the plaintiff.

fields.label: Use This (defense perspective)
fields.definition: Battery findings the defense can actively use, ordered from most to least useful from the defense's perspective. Reveals the defense's playbook for this pair — what findings they will exploit and how. Knowing this allows the prosecution's team to anticipate and counter those moves.
fields.why_it_matters: Reveals exactly what the defense sees as their usable assets in this pair. The prosecution's team can use this to anticipate which findings the defense will emphasize, and prepare their responses accordingly.
fields.value_description: An ordered list of findings the defense can actively use. Each item shows a utility level (low, medium, or high), which call and field it came from, and a brief explanation of why it is useful to the defense.

enum_values.high: This finding is a significant strategic asset for the defense. They will prioritize it and the prosecution's team needs to prepare a response.
enum_values.medium: This finding is moderately useful to the defense. They may incorporate it into their strategy and the prosecution should be aware of it.
enum_values.low: This finding has limited strategic value for the defense. They may note it but it is unlikely to drive their strategy.

fields.null_explanation: No usable findings were identified for this pair from the defense's perspective.

fields.label: Watch This (defense perspective)
fields.definition: Battery findings that represent risk or threat to the defense's side, ordered from highest to lowest threat. These are the defense's vulnerabilities in this pair — what they are afraid of and how they plan to mitigate it. Directly useful to the prosecution's team because it shows exactly where to press.
fields.why_it_matters: Surfaces the defense's own risk assessment for this pair. When the defense identifies something as a high threat to their position, that is precisely where the prosecution's team should focus. The mitigation strategies show how the defense plans to protect themselves — and where those protections might be challenged.
fields.value_description: An ordered list of risks the defense faces in this pair, from highest to lowest threat. Each item shows a threat level, which call and field it came from, and the defense's mitigation strategy.

enum_values.high: This finding poses a significant threat to the defense's position. They consider it a serious vulnerability and have a mitigation plan — the prosecution's team should press here.
enum_values.medium: This finding poses a moderate threat to the defense. They are aware of it and plan to manage it but it is not their primary concern.
enum_values.low: This finding poses a minor threat to the defense. They do not consider it a significant vulnerability.

fields.null_explanation: No significant threats were identified for this pair from the defense's perspective.

fields.label: Call Rank (defense perspective)
fields.definition: All six calls from the source battery ranked 1 through 6 by strategic importance for this specific pair from the defense's perspective. Reveals which analytical dimensions the defense considers most valuable for their position on this pair — where their strategic focus lies.
fields.why_it_matters: Shows where the defense's analytical priority falls on this pair. When the defense ranks a call highly, they see significant strategic value in that dimension — meaning the prosecution's team should pay close attention to what that call produced and be prepared to counter the defense's use of it.
fields.value_description: All six calls are shown ranked from most to least strategically important for this pair from the defense's perspective. Each rank includes a one-sentence explanation of why that call was ranked where it was.
